name: Renal Tubular Acidosis Type 3
aliases: Combined Proximal and Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Proximal and Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap
Evidence of proximal tubular bicarbonate wasting (e.g., decreased bicarbonate reabsorption)
Impaired distal tubular acidification demonstrated by inability to acidify urine (urine pH >5.5) despite systemic acidosis
Presence of hypokalemia due to renal potassium wasting
Preserved glomerular filtration rate with tubular dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap plus evidence of both proximal bicarbonate wasting and distal acidification defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of metabolic acidosis and confirmation by laboratory testing of tubular function.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap
Impaired urinary acidification (urine pH >5.5 despite systemic acidosis)

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to electrolyte imbalance

laboratory: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap
Inability to acidify urine (urine pH >5.5) despite systemic acidosis
Normal or near-normal glomerular filtration rate
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis
Bone X-rays showing signs of osteomalacia or rickets in children
genetic: Mutations affecting carbonic anhydrase II gene (CA2) in some cases
Other genetic defects affecting proximal and distal tubular acid-base transporters

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated distal acidification defect without proximal bicarbonate wasting
Urine acidification intact in distal tubule
Urine pH can be <5.5 after acid load
Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction with glucosuria, aminoaciduria, and phosphaturia
More extensive tubular defects beyond acid-base handling

redFlags: Severe hypokalemia causing muscle paralysis or arrhythmias
Failure to thrive or severe growth retardation in children
references: Karet FE. Renal tubular acidosis. Annu Rev Med. 2009;60:233-247.
Batlle DC, Haque SK. Genetic causes and mechanisms of distal renal tubular acidosis. Nephrol Dial Transplant. 2012;27(10):3691-3704.
